Context: the owner asked for a forecasting part. The specification lists forecasting nowhere and excludes trading strategies and P&L backtests (§4). The scaling laws predict the roughness of volatility from order flow (H_σ = 2 H0 − 3/2); roughness is known to matter for volatility forecasts (Gatheral, Jaisson & Rosenbaum, 2018, §5). The 5-year daily history of ADR 0011 gives enough days for rolling out-of-sample forecasts.

Decision:

  • A separate family of hypotheses F1–F3 (pre-registration §10), evaluated with statistical losses only: QLIKE (primary) and squared error on the level of the h-day average, Diebold–Mariano tests pooled across pairs, model confidence set per pair. No trading rule.
  • The principal rough model is the exact Gaussian predictor of the model the Whittle estimator already fits (day-averaged fBm plus white noise), parameters by Whittle on a 500-day window. The published GJR kernel is kept as a benchmark (rough_gjr): in a probe it lost 13 % of one-step MSE to the exact predictor on daily-sampled fBm, and more with noise, so making it the rough model would test the discretisation, not roughness.
  • Log forecasts become levels with each model's own lognormal correction; Duan smearing stays as an option. In probes, smearing of overlapping 22-day targets cost the exact predictor about 10 % of QLIKE against 0.5 % for the lognormal correction.
  • The theory link (F2) compares H fixed at 2 Ĥ0 − 3/2 with H fixed at the development estimate of H_σ, everything else equal; on the confirmation sample both use only the development sample, so the test is out of sample. On the development sample these rows are flagged look_ahead.
  • The daily history gains the traded quote volume and trade count (stage history_rv 3, before any history file existed), for the volume target F3.
  • forecast is excluded from the checkpoint key of the simulation study: it does not change a simulated cell, and the full study was running when the section was added.

Consequences: one more command (ofs forecast), outputs in data/forecast/, three API endpoints, a dashboard page, a report table and figure. Forecasting adds about one CPU-hour per sample with 120 series. The probes behind the two design choices are summarised in docs/forecasting.md; the reproducible check is ofs simulate forecast.

docs.title: ADR 0014 — Continuous L2 collector: sampled books, every trade, two connections
docs.text:
Status: accepted (2026-11-10)

Context: the specification lists a continuous WebSocket collector of perpetual L2 data as an extension (§4), for a propagator model of impact. Full diff-depth at 100 ms is about ten messages a second per symbol; storing every message is possible but heavy, and a book rebuilt from diffs is only valid while the update-id sequence is unbroken.

Decision:

  • Keep a local book per symbol with Binance's rules (snapshot, bridge U ≤ L ≤ u, then pu = previous u), rebuild on any gap or crossed book, and sample it every second (top 20 levels plus best quotes, spread, microprice, imbalance, depth within 10 bps) rather than storing raw diffs. Record every aggregated trade.
  • Two WebSocket connections: depth on /public, trades on /market. Checked on 2026-11-10, the legacy root accepts an aggTrade subscription and sends nothing.
  • Hourly Parquet files, atomic writes, part files after a restart; no pipeline lock.
  • Opt-in compose profile l2 (three perpetuals by default): the collector needs an always-on machine, which the laptop is not.

Consequences: about 15 MB a day for three perpetuals; the propagator study can align trades and books on milliseconds. Raw diffs are not kept, so a finer sampling needs a new run. Sampling at 1 s hides sub-second book dynamics, which the trades still show.

docs.title: ADR 0015 — H0 on the order flow centred day by day in proportion to volume
docs.text:
Status: accepted (2026-11-12). Amends ADR 0008 point (1) and its negative control; recorded as deviations D3 and D4 (config/deviations.md).

Context: on the development year (2024-11-01 to 2025-10-31, 60 spot and 59 USD-M pairs) the shuffled-sign negative control failed. The pre-registered expectation is H0 = 1/2. The principal estimator gave 0.80 on spot and 0.79 on USD-M (0 of 60 spot pairs within 0.05 of 0.5). The sign-autocorrelation version gave 1.00 everywhere.

  • The sign-autocorrelation control cannot work: shuffled signs have a flat autocorrelation, a power law fitted to it has exponent 0, and H0 = 1 − γ/2 = 1 by construction.
  • The flow control failed because of how it was centred. The shuffle permutes signs within each day, so each day keeps its net imbalance m_d = net flow / volume, about 5 % of volume on BTC. The shuffled flow therefore drifts in proportion to traded volume: m_d · V per window. The control removed the day's mean increment, a drift uniform in time, which leaves m_d (V − mean V). That residue inherits the clustering of trading activity and reads as memory.
  • The same drift is in the real flow, which the principal did not centre at all (ADR 0008: "the daily net imbalance is part of the memory"). In simulation, signs with no memory but a random daily imbalance of sd 5 % give H0 ≈ 0.97–0.99 with that estimator.
  • The simulation study and the property test missed both problems because their trades arrive uniformly in time with independent sizes. With no activity clustering, the two centrings agree.

Measured on 10-second bins of the development year (same fit as the principal; raw flows):

Pair real, uncentred real, volume-centred shuffled, time-centred shuffled, volume-centred BTC spot 0.707 0.622 0.862 0.498 BTC USD-M 0.608 0.600 0.684 0.499 ETH spot 0.696 0.656 0.826 0.491 ETH USD-M 0.617 0.607 0.859 0.498 DOGE spot 0.684 0.648 0.871 0.493 DOGE USD-M 0.601 0.576 0.775 0.490 LINK spot 0.719 0.696 0.821 0.499 LINK USD-M 0.626 0.561 0.811 0.498

Simulation (30 days × 30,000 trades, lognormal sizes, two seeds; "clustered" = window intensity exp(fBm)):

Signs (true H0) Activity uncentred volume-centred shuffled, time-centred shuffled, volume-centred no memory, daily imbalance sd 5 % (0.5) uniform 0.973 0.500 0.504 0.499 no memory, daily imbalance sd 5 % (0.5) clustered 0.989 0.497 0.929 0.498 Lillo–Mike–Farmer (0.7, asymptotic) uniform 0.797 0.779 0.501 0.500 Lillo–Mike–Farmer (0.7, asymptotic) clustered 0.775 0.753 0.894 0.499

Decision:

  1. The volume-centred flow. The reducer removes each day's imbalance from every window in proportion to the window's volume: F − (ΣF / ΣV) V. It does so for the signed flow (deseasonalised and raw) and for the shuffled flow. It stores the variance sums in their own table, flow_var_vc, with a version of its own (flow_vc), so adding it did not recompute the other pass-2 statistics.
  2. The principal (mixed_fbm_vc) fits the mixed fBm to that flow, and so do its window, no-seasonality and τmax variants, the control (quadratic-variation ratio) and the diagnostics. Removing the day's net increment shrinks the variance at large τ like a bridge. With constant activity the expected mean squared increment of lag m, out of N windows, is exactly g_H(m) = m^{2H} − 2 (m/N) A(m) + (m/N)² N^{2H}, where A(m) = [Σ_{u=N−m+1..N} u^{2H} − Σ_{u=1..m−1} u^{2H}] / (N − m + 1). For H = 1/2 this is the Brownian bridge m (1 − m/N). The fit uses g_H and g_{1/2} instead of the pure powers. They are tabulated on a grid of H and interpolated by a spline; a fit takes about 10 ms.
  3. The negative control is the same fit on the shuffled, volume-centred flow. The shuffled sign autocorrelation becomes a diagnostic.
  4. The pre-registered principal stays in the specification curve as the H0 variant uncentred.

Checks: g_H equals the exact covariance of a centred fBm to machine precision (unit test). On simulated fGn centred day by day, with 60 days, the bridge-aware fit recovers H:

True H Centred, plain fit Centred, bridge-aware fit 0.7 0.680 0.702 0.8 0.770 0.803 0.9 0.867 0.901

A property test with clustered activity and a daily imbalance but no memory requires H0 = 1/2 for both the signed and the shuffled volume-centred flow. The H0 cells of the simulation study are re-run with the new principal (scenario version 2), and the pre-registered acceptance rule decides.

Consequences:

  • H0 measures within-day persistence of the flow net of each day's imbalance. A day-level imbalance, which the uncentred estimator counted as memory, no longer counts.
  • On the 8 pair-markets above, H0 drops by 0.01–0.085 (median 0.03).
  • With genuine memory the centring removes part of the low-frequency signal, and the bridge-aware fit corrects that exactly under constant activity.
  • Under clustered activity the correction is approximate. The remaining effect, about 0.02 in the Lillo–Mike–Farmer simulation, is within the simulation's tolerance and is measured by the re-run study.
  • Every development-sample estimate, test and forecast that uses H0 is recomputed before the config-frozen tag.

Outcome on the development year (re-run of 2026-11-14, all 119 pair-markets):

  • The negative control has a median of 0.500 on spot and 0.499 on USD-M, with 90 % and 97 % of the pairs within 0.05 of 1/2. The rest are fits without a fractional part, whose intervals contain 1/2.
  • H0 hardly moves on spot (median 0.704 against 0.699) and falls on USD-M (0.584 against 0.619). The estimate on 8 pair-markets above had suggested a fall of 0.03 on both markets.
  • On 27 of the 59 USD-M pairs, and on no spot pair, the fit puts no weight on the Brownian part: the variance of the centred flow is a single power law from 10 seconds to four hours. The quadratic-variation ratio falls with the window on USD-M (median 0.64 at 10 seconds, 0.60 at 60 seconds), so the exponent depends on the time scale there. The mixed model of the theory fits the spot flow better than the perpetual one (median log error 0.05 against 0.12).
  • Three decisions of the development tests changed, in both directions: H1 on USD-M from undecided to compatible, H3 on both markets from undecided to rejected (config/deviations.md, D4).

docs.title: ADR 0016 — Monthly packs of the daily statistics
docs.text:
Status: accepted (2026-11-17)

Context: ADR 0002 writes one file per statistic, pair and day. Two years of 119 pair-markets and 11 statistics made about 955,000 files of a few kilobytes each. On the laptop's hard disk the daily cycle of 2026-11-15 took about 11 hours, nearly all of it spent opening those files: the rolling estimates read 8,030 files per pair, and the weekly regime monitor read all 11 statistics when it needs one. Each file is also one request for the weekly backup (Cloudflare R2's free tier counts a million uploads a month) and one entry to copy when the data move to a server.

Decision: once a month can no longer change in normal operation (it ends more than max(catchup_days, recheck_days) + 5 days before the run's day: outside the daily replay and the weekly recheck), its per-day files are folded into one pack per statistic, pair and month, {YYYY-MM}__pack.parquet, whose Parquet metadata lists the days it holds and the version of each (ofs.packs). The weekly run packs the months that just closed; ofs compact packs everything. Writers keep writing per-day files, so ADR 0002 holds unchanged:

  • a per-day file shadows the pack's rows for its day (it is newer: a manual backfill, a version bump); the next compaction folds it in;
  • a day is done at a version when its per-day file at that version exists, or when it has no per-day file and the pack holds it at that version;
  • invalidating a day (ofs recheck) deletes its per-day files and rewrites the pack without it;
  • compaction writes the pack atomically, reads it back and compares it with the per-day files, and only then deletes them; an interruption leaves per-day files that shadow identical rows.

Only the 11 statistics the estimators read are packed. The windows (bins_*), the seasonal sums and the 5-year history keep their layout. The regime monitor now loads only what the principal H0 estimator reads (H0_KINDS: 3 of the 11 statistics).

Consequences: readers get exactly the frames they got from per-day files (one frame per day, in date order). This was checked on real data before the conversion: for five pair-markets, every statistic read from packs over the 23 closed months equalled the per-day read, and the regime monitor gave the same blocks from 3 statistics as from 11 (and the same as its last stored run). Opening a rolling window reads about 11 × (23 packs + 47 days) files instead of 8,030; the 955,000 files become about 30,000 packs plus the open months' per-day files. A month packed by mistake while still open stays correct (per-day files shadow it); the price is one rewrite of the pack at the next compaction.

docs.title: 2026-11-09: A cleanup command deleted derived data
docs.text:
Cause: before restarting the backfill, temporary files were removed with Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath data -Recurse -Include '*.part','*.tmp-*' | Remove-Item; Windows PowerShell 5.1 does not apply -Include together with -LiteralPath, so the command deleted every file it reached for about 13 minutes before it was stopped: in alphabetical order, all the 1-second and 10-second windows, the validation cache and most day_summary files; the ten other daily statistics tables, the validation reports, the manifest and the logs were not reached.

Fix: ofs clean-temp (with --dry-run) matches each file name in Python and deletes only *.tmp-* and *.part; operations use it instead of shell filters. The stages are idempotent: the restarted backfill finds pass 1 incomplete, downloads the raw files again from Binance Vision and rewrites the windows and day_summary (pass 2, intact, is kept); about eight hours of downloads were redone, nothing was lost.

Test added: tests/unit/test_misc.py::test_only_temporary_files_are_cleaned

docs.title: 2026-11-09: Re-published files not applied downstream
docs.text:
Cause: ofs ingest --recheck downloaded files whose .CHECKSUM had changed, but the day was already reduced, so its statistics kept coming from the old file; the daily run also never replayed a day that was missing at 12:00 UTC (found while auditing the pipeline against spec §6.4 and §11.4).

Fix: ofs recheck invalidates and recomputes every output of a corrected day and pass 2 of its neighbours; the daily run replays a 7-day window and applies re-published files weekly (ADR 0010).

Test added: tests/unit/test_reduce_pipeline.py::test_republished_file_is_applied_downstream, tests/unit/test_cli_daily.py::test_daily_replays_a_file_published_late

docs.title: 2026-11-09: fGn embedding failed at H = 0.9 and a study run was lost
docs.text:
Cause: the fGn autocovariance was computed as a plain second difference, which subtracts numbers of order 1e11 at lags of millions; the 365-day simulations at H = 0.9 got a negative circulant embedding and raised. run_study then stopped saving at the first failing cell while the process pool kept computing every queued cell, so 8 hours of the full study were lost.

Fix: cancellation-free autocovariance (expm1/log1p), exact white noise at H = 0.5; a failing cell is now logged (cell_failed) and the others are still checkpointed; the checkpoint key leaves out the settings decided from the study (roles, calibration factor, sample split).

Test added: tests/simulation/test_simulators.py::test_embedding_of_a_long_persistent_series_is_valid

docs.title: 2026-11-09: Futures kline open convention
docs.text:
Cause: the OHLC check compared the kline open with the first trade of the minute, but USD-M klines open at the previous minute's last price when the first trade comes a few milliseconds after the boundary; the NEIROUSDT perpetual of 2024-11-07 (8/1440 minutes, up to 10 ticks) was blocked although its data were correct.

Fix: the open is compared with the first trade of the minute and with the last trade before it (ADR 0009 amendment, validation stage version 2); blocked days keep their raw file and are re-validated by ofs reduce.

Test added: tests/unit/test_validate.py::test_ohlc_open_at_previous_close

docs.title: 2026-11-09: Manifest late null column
docs.text:
Cause: the first real one-day backfill crashed when writing the manifest: polars inferred the error column from the first 100 records (all null), then met "HTTP 404" (pairs not listed yet).

Fix: the manifest frame is built with the explicit schema of the contract; the other frames built from lists of rows read the whole list to infer types.

Test added: tests/unit/test_download.py::test_manifest_accepts_a_late_error

docs.title: 2026-11-09: Network error labelled delisted
docs.text:
Cause: explain_missing relabelled network errors after the last available day as delisted, which would hide a failed download of the latest day from the O1 count.

Fix: only 404s (missing) are explained by the listing dates; errors stay unexplained until a retry succeeds.

Test added: tests/unit/test_download.py::test_manifest_explain_missing

docs.title: 2026-11-09: Perpetual klines without trades
docs.text:
Cause: the universe measured availability on daily klines, but the RAYUSDT perpetual has 1-minute klines through 2026 and no aggTrades after 2022-11-15, so a perpetual with no trades in the window was attached (found on the first real day: aggTrades 404, klines 200).

Fix: availability of the spot pair and of the perpetual is counted on the daily aggTrades files of the S3 listing; the rebuilt universe keeps the same 60 pairs, RAYUSDT without a perpetual (57 perpetuals).

Test added: tests/unit/test_universe.py::test_build_universe_ranks_filters_and_maps_perps (klines-only symbol and perpetual)

docs.title: 2026-11-09: Universe build without retries
docs.text:
Cause: rebuilding the universe (about 10 000 requests to the S3 listing and the monthly klines) failed on one dropped connection ("Server disconnected without sending a response"): unlike the downloader, the universe builder had no retry.

Fix: every request of the universe builder goes through the downloader's policy (5 attempts, exponential back-off, on transport errors and 408/425/429/5xx).

Test added: tests/unit/test_universe.py::test_build_universe_ranks_filters_and_maps_perps (a dropped connection then a 503 before the first listing)

docs.title: 2026-11-09: Unpublished trade ids block perpetual days
docs.text:
Cause: the continuity check blocked days above 0.1 % of missing trade ids; USD-M files miss 0.1-0.3 % of their trade ids from mid-2025 (fills never published, aggTrade ids consecutive), so 49 perpetual days were already blocked by 2025-05 and most later ones would have been (found by the real-day benchmark of BTCUSDT on 2025-10-10).

Fix: block on missing aggTrade rows, on a run of more than 1000 missing trade ids, or above 2 % (ADR 0012, validation stage version 3); the blocked days kept their raw files and were validated again.

Test added: tests/unit/test_validate.py::test_unpublished_trade_ids_do_not_block, tests/unit/test_validate.py::test_missing_rows_and_large_holes_block

docs.title: 2026-11-10: A restart stopped the long jobs, and the resume was slow
docs.text:
Cause: the development machine was restarted from the Windows menu at 23:15, which ended the detached backfill and the two jobs waiting on it (the earlier lid close of 03:14 had done the same). On relaunch, the resume script first ran ofs clean-temp; walking about a million partition files took more than 30 minutes, while holding the data lock that the backfill needs, so nothing downloaded during that time.

Fix: the resume script relaunches the jobs immediately; leftover *.tmp-* and *.part files are harmless (no reader matches them: every table is read through *.parquet) and are cleaned later with ofs clean-temp when no job is writing. Finished days and simulation cells are skipped on resume, so the restart cost about an hour of downloads and nothing else. Operations: on the production VM the jobs run in containers with restart: unless-stopped; a laptop must not be restarted or closed during a backfill.

Second occurrence: on 2026-11-11 at 04:42, after Windows had installed an update during the night, the machine was restarted again from the Start menu; the jobs stopped for eight hours until the next check. The relaunched backfill then spent about a minute per finished week just to skip it: each (pair, market) group read its 84-day seasonal profile before finding that every day was already reduced. process_group now reads the profile only when a day still needs pass 2, which turns the skip into a few file-existence checks. Operations: pause Windows Update while long jobs run.

Third occurrence: on 2026-11-11 at 16:23, without any restart, every job process (the backfill, its ofs worker and the two waiting runners) ended in the same second, with no error in their logs. The event logs show a heavy interactive program starting on the machine three minutes earlier, and the same sequence on 2026-11-10 at 21:53 followed by the backfill stopping at 22:00 (that stop had been attributed to the 23:15 restart, which only found it already dead). Whether the processes were ended by hand or by that program is not established. The jobs now start at below-normal priority, which their child processes inherit, so an interactive program keeps the CPU it needs; resume costs a few minutes since the skip fix.

Fourth occurrence: on 2026-11-12 at 11:20, with no restart and no game client running, both job trees then running ended within two seconds (the simulation study and the reduction of the volume-centred statistics, runners included). The reduction's ofs process reported exit code 0xC000013A, which is a console control event (Ctrl+C, close). Its runner was set to ignore Ctrl+C and still ended right after it, so the consoles were most likely closed: a close event cannot be ignored. Three idle test processes, started the same way the day before with consoles of their own, were not touched. Twenty-four seconds later the user cancelled a scheduled defragmentation of the data disk, which had been slowing the reduction. The fix removes the consoles altogether: the runners now start under pythonw.exe (no console) and launch ofs with CREATE_NO_WINDOW (a hidden console its pool workers inherit). There is then no window to close, and no console event can reach a job. Finished cells and days were skipped on resume, so the stop cost about 30 minutes.

Fifth occurrence: on 2026-11-12 at 23:02 and on 2026-11-13 at 13:01 the laptop was shut down while the development estimates were running. Estimates were written only once every pair was done, so each shutdown lost the whole run. Each restart then spent close to two hours before its first pair, reading the realised variance of every pair to classify the volatility regimes: 43,000 small files on a cold hard disk. run_estimates now saves each pair-market as soon as it is computed, and the regimes with them, in a folder named after everything the results depend on (sample, days, replications, configuration, code version). A restarted run reads them back and computes only what is missing, so a shutdown costs the pairs in flight, about fifteen minutes. Operations: a commit, or a change to a tracked file, changes the code version and makes a restarted run start over, so the repository is left untouched while an estimation runs; work in progress goes to a separate worktree.

Cause of the third and fourth occurrences, found on 2026-11-14: the antivirus. Avast's Do Not Disturb mode (its log calls it game mode) starts whenever a full-screen program comes to the front, which includes the code editor and media players, and applies a rule named PauseSystemBackgroundTasks. Its log shows that rule being switched on or off in the same minute as every unexplained stop (2026-11-10 22:00, 2026-11-11 16:23 and 16:29), and two seconds after the one timed to the second (2026-11-12 11:20:30). The same rule disables scheduled tasks while it is active, which is why the logon task that relaunches the jobs was found disabled three times. How the rule ends console processes is not established; the jobs have run without a console since 2026-11-12 and have survived every activation since. Operations: switch that mode off on a machine that runs long jobs, and check the state of the relaunch task when checking the jobs.

Tests added: tests/unit/test_registry_run.py::test_run_estimates_resumes_from_checkpoints (a stopped run resumes without recomputing a saved pair or re-reading the regimes); the reader side of temporary files is covered by tests/unit/test_misc.py::test_only_temporary_files_are_cleaned.

docs.title: 2026-11-15: Forked pool workers hang on Linux
docs.text:
Cause: every process pool used the platform's default start method. On Linux that is fork, and a worker forked while a thread of polars, numba or the BLAS holds a lock waits for ever. Development ran on Windows, where workers are spawned, so nothing showed. It was found by running the CI job in a Linux container before the first push: the test suite stopped, using no CPU, on the only test that reduces a range of days with two jobs. The daily pipeline in its container and the weekly simulation job would have frozen the same way.

Fix: ofs.utils.process_pool builds every pool with the spawn context (estimates, forecasts, forecast simulation, reduction, simulation study). The CI job is now rehearsed in a Linux container before a push that changes how processes or files are handled.

Test added: tests/unit/test_misc.py::test_process_pools_spawn_their_workers

docs.title: 2026-11-15: The health check read every validation report
docs.text:
Cause: GET /health counted the pair-days blocked by validation by reading every validation report, about 86,000 small files for two years. In the container, on a read-only mount of the data, the request had not answered after 400 s, while the health check of docker-compose.yml allows 10 s every minute: the API would have been marked unhealthy for ever. The unit tests ran on a handful of files and could not see it.

Fix: the daily run records the count in the status file (Store.validation_failures reads the reports once a day); Store.health returns the recorded number, or null before the first run, and reads only the status file and the manifest. The dashboard's health page read the same reports to list the failures and did not render in the container either: it now reads them on demand (a switch on the page), and a cached table is served even when the data are mounted read-only and the cache cannot be rewritten.

Test added: tests/unit/test_api_store.py::test_health_reports_the_count_the_daily_run_recorded, tests/unit/test_misc.py::test_cached_table_is_served_when_the_cache_cannot_be_written

docs.title: 2026-11-15: The paper had never been compiled
docs.text:
Cause: the development machine had no LaTeX and the weekly CI job that compiles the paper had not run yet, so paper/main.tex had only ever been read. The first compilation stopped on two errors: \Hz_i expands to H_0_i (double subscript), and the link colour blue!50!black needs the package xcolor. Three generated tables were also 70 to 85 pt wider than the page.

Fix: H_{0,i} written out, xcolor loaded; every generated table sits in an adjustbox that shrinks it only when it is wider than the text; slide figures fit both the height and the width of their column. Paper and slides now compile without an overfull box, locally with Tectonic and in the weekly job.

Test added: none in the test suite; the weekly CI job compiles both documents.

docs.title: 2026-11-15: A truncated download stopped the venue comparison
docs.text:
Cause: one daily file of Bybit's archive arrived truncated four times in a row. A connection closed early ends HTTPResponse.read(amt) without an error, so only the gzip check noticed, with an EOFError. After the retries that error was raised again and reached the command line, where click takes it for the end of input at a prompt: the command printed "Aborted.", exited 1 without a traceback, and the comparison stopped at 239 of 300 days.

Fix: the size is compared with Content-Length and the gzip stream is read to its end; after five attempts the day counts as failed (DownloadError) and is skipped, the run goes on, and a later run tries the day again. The comparison reports the days used.

Test added: tests/unit/test_venues.py::test_a_file_that_cannot_be_fetched_skips_its_day
